paper.title: Equivalence of Context and Parameter Updates in Modern Transformer Blocks

claims.scope: One full Gemma 3 1B layer/token plus five seeded toy trials and negative controls.
Sequential construction through all 26 Gemma layers for one target history and token.

claims.paper_claim: Controllability framework across modern Transformer blocks
claims.scope: 40 trials across eight actual pinned Transformers class forms with topology, NumPy, and nonzero-input controls.

claims.paper_claim: Exact float32 and naive-bfloat16 agreement percentages
claims.scope: Under the pinned five-prompt/100-token CPU protocol, naive bfloat16 is 100/100 rather than the paper's exact 87.5%.
Naive and stable bfloat16 both reach 100/100; stable lowers worst logit error from 0.375 to 0.25.
Gemma, Llama, Falcon, Mistral, Mixtral, Qwen, GPT-2, and GPT-J at reduced deterministic widths.

limitations: Theorem proofs, universal hardware behavior, all checkpoints, image/Falcon studies, and every ablation are not reproduced.
The Gemma evidence is one-checkpoint and token-specific; it does not establish arbitrary-query reuse.
Architecture routes other than Gemma use reduced-width random weights and are architecture-level evidence.
The historical 2/12 judge score is provenance only; no new score or author endorsement is claimed.
